The [original SASRec implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kang205/SASRec/master/model.py) and [PyTorch implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pmixer/SASRec.pytorch/main/python/model.py) multiply input item embeddings by √d, add positional embeddings, apply embedding dropout, and finish with LayerNorm; scoring uses the same item table without √d scaling. Consequently, residual strength depends on whether r_t uses raw, scaled, normalized, or dropped embeddings. Architectural inference: adding after final LayerNorm bypasses that normalization and changes both query direction and norm; adding before it changes direction through normalization. LayerNorm has learned affine parameters, so it does not guarantee unit L2 norm. With tied scoring, q_t·e_i = h_t·e_i + αr_t·e_i: the residual directly adds an item-similarity score and introduces another gradient path into the shared table.

Recommended controls, inferred from these mechanics: define r_t using only nonpadding inputs at positions ≤t, predicting the item at t+1; use identical logic during training and inference. Compare α=0, raw versus normalized residuals, and addition before versus after final LayerNorm, with matched normalization-only baselines. Explicitly control dropout on the residual branch. Isolate directional gains using q′_t=||h_t||₂q_t/(||q_t||₂+ε), and test a baseline with matched logit temperature during training. Positive query scaling alone cannot change a fixed query’s ranking, but changes training gradients and calibration. Compare recent-item residuals against equal-norm shuffled-history or older-item residuals; detach residual embeddings to probe the extra gradient path. Track query/item norms, residual-to-hidden norm ratios, cosine alignment, logit spread, and validation HR@10 under identical seeds and candidates. Treat these as proposed ablations, not established performance gains.
